question: How to handle short prompts (<128 tokens) where the hot window includes prompt tokens from P node?

analysis.long_prompts_over_128: Hot window (128 tokens) covers only decode-generated tokens. D computes PROLOG for each new token locally, writes BF16 ring locally. No P-to-D BF16 transfer needed. GPQA questions are all >128 tokens, so this is the common case.
analysis.short_prompts_under_128: Hot window would include some prompt tokens. These tokens' KV was computed on P (during prefill). Their BF16 exists only on P. D needs P-to-D BF16 transfer to fill the hot window for these tokens. Without transfer, the hot window would be incomplete for the prompt portion.

options_for_short_prompts.A_fallback_to_c4: When prompt < 128 tokens, fall back to normal C4 for the prompt portion of the hot window. BF16 only for decode-generated tokens. Simple but loses precision benefit for short prompts.
options_for_short_prompts.B_partial_hot_window: Only use BF16 for the tokens that have BF16 available (decode tokens). Prompt portion stays C4. Hot window is partially BF16, partially C4.
options_for_short_prompts.C_pd_transfer: Implement P-to-D BF16 tail window transfer. P snapshots the last 128 tokens' BF16 at prefill completion and transfers alongside regular KV. Full BF16 hot window even for short prompts. Most correct but requires PD lifecycle (Step 5).
options_for_short_prompts.D_eager_recompute: D recomputes BF16 for prompt tokens when it detects missing hot window data. Wasteful (duplicate KV projection) but correct. Probably rejected per 'no second projection' rule.

recommended_approach: Start with option A or B for initial verification (GPQA has long prompts, so this is edge case). Implement option C (PD transfer) later for full production coverage. Option D violates no-duplicate-compute constraint.
user_question: User asks: is fallback acceptable for short prompts, or should we implement PD transfer from the start? What is the recommended handling?
